title: Lloyd's algorithm and EM for a Gaussian mixture
brief: Implement k-means with k-means++ seeding, then EM for a Gaussian mixture, and watch k-means fall out as its zero-variance limit.
hints: kmeans_objective and the assignment step both use ||x - c||^2 = ||x||^2 - 2 x.c + ||c||^2; the ||x||^2 term is the same for every center, so you can drop it when finding the argmin.
In lloyd, an empty cluster after reassignment should keep its previous center rather than averaging zero points into a NaN.

kmeans_plusplus_init: track the squared distance from every point to its nearest chosen center, update it with a running minimum as each new center is added, and normalise it to a probability vector for rng.choice.

gmm_e_step: work with log(weights[j]) + log N(x_i; mean_j, cov_j) for every component, subtract the per-row maximum before exponentiating, and recover the log-likelihood as max + log(sum of the shifted exponentials).
gmm_m_step's covariance update is a responsibility-weighted outer product: sum_i r_ij (x_i - mu_j)(x_i - mu_j)^T / sum_i r_ij, plus reg_covar times the identity.
